evidence.fit: Both audiences get a pass: the headline and the 03:14 'Break · 22 min left' phone speak to the nurse; 'For nurse managers: You see the swap before it happens' and a 'Who buys it / Who uses it' block speak to the buyer. 'What Swaptide doesn't do' (doesn't approve swaps, doesn't change your rules, doesn't handle payroll) and the FAQ meet the constraints cleanly, and the pilot box is honest. But the manager section is three icon cards plus a static mock, so it reads closer to a generic scheduling SaaS page than something that understands a 12-hour shift beyond a few times of day.

reason: As the nurse manager, A answers my real doubt (will this respect my limits and leave the decision to me?) by letting me run Priya's Saturday swap through Dana and Marcus, see the exact rule each one breaks, and change my own limits, all labelled as sample data. B is honest and pleasant and its headline speaks better to the nurse on a break, but it shows the product only as pictures with dead Approve buttons and unlabelled names. I would change my mind only if B shipped a working, labelled demo and A kept hiding the nurse line on phones.
